title: Type safety, and enums with fields

blocks.value: **Using enums makes values type-safe.** *Type-safe* describes a data type that allows only appropriate behaviors.

**As with other classes, you can also add methods and other fields to an enum type.** This is where enums become powerful: the pizza example above keeps prices in a `switch`, far away from the sizes they belong to. Put them together:

Regular    381.00  (with VAT   426.72)
Large      602.00  (with VAT   674.24)
Party      799.00  (with VAT   894.88)
No `switch` at all. Each constant carries its own data, the VAT rule is written once, and adding a new size means adding **one line**: with no chance of forgetting to update a switch somewhere else.
